answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by starting each identity on a bare tundra: zero trust, only low-value tasks. Trust accrues like a glacier, one honest countersign at a time, and only a crystal-growth threshold converts that accumulated honesty into privilege. The cost lands on the attacker, not the protocol. Every fake identity must repeat the same slow accretion alone, so mass sybils cost mass effort, while each early-stage upside stays capped below what it spent.
